device.name: mano_pybullet HandLiftEnv-v1 (PyBullet MANO hand lifting an object)

facts.text: HandLiftEnv-v1 is registered as a gym environment with entry point mano_pybullet.envs:HandLiftEnv
HandLiftEnv is the object-lifting subclass of HandObjectEnv
The default target lift height is 0.25
The target height is stored in _target_height at construction
The reward is the z coordinate of the object's base position
The episode is done when the object's z coordinate is greater than the target height
HandLiftEnv passes itself as the model_path argument of HandObjectEnv
The default hand side is the right hand (HAND_RIGHT = 1) and the default control mode is joint space (MODE_JOINT = 1)
The default constructor selects hand_side=HAND_RIGHT and control_mode=MODE_JOINT
In joint mode the action per hand is a 3-vector base position bounded by -5.0 to 5.0, a 4-vector base quaternion bounded by -1.0 to 1.0, and the hand model's joint angles

The observation per hand is a 3-vector base position, a 4-vector base quaternion, a 6-vector constraint force bounded by -10.0 to 10.0, the joint angles, joint velocities bounded by -3.0 to 3.0 and joint torques bounded by -1.0 to 1.0
HandObjectEnv extends the observation space with the object's 3-vector base position and 4-vector base quaternion
The hand state is the base position, base orientation, constraint forces, joint positions, joint velocities and joint torques
HandModel20 is a heuristic rigid model with 20 degrees of freedom
The dofs_limits property returns the lower and upper limit of every model degree of freedom
The metadata declares step_time 1.0 / 60.0 seconds
step() runs int(step_time * 240.0) simulation steps and returns observation, reward, done, info
reset() sets gravity (0, 0, -10) and deterministicOverlappingPairs=1
The gym extra installs gym>=0.17.3 and imageio, and the package requires numpy, chumpy, transforms3d and pybullet>=3.0.6
The MANO models must be downloaded separately from the MANO website and pointed to by MANO_MODELS_DIR
The README describes HandLiftEnv as the environment whose target is to lift an object

determinism.notes: the default construction does not randomize the hand shape, reset() enables deterministic overlapping pairs, and the bridge records the seed (the environment's own RNG is used only when randomize_hand_shape is enabled); the bridge reports exact determinism only when the environment exposes get_state/set_state, which this one does not

gaps: rigid-body PyBullet simulation: contact, friction, damping and actuator parameters are those of the engine and the hand model, not of a physical hand; the model was not validated against a device
the fake backend is kinematic: the object follows the commanded hand base position and the joint angles only shape the observation; it runs no PyBullet, contact or gravity solver

the upstream HandLiftEnv constructor passes the environment object as model_path to HandObjectEnv (mano_pybullet/envs/hand_lift_env.py:17), so the upstream simulator path was not run and is not reproduced by the fake
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0; ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state
the fake models the default right hand with the 20 degrees of freedom of HandModel20, not the optional HandModel45 or the left/both-hand configurations
the action and observation spaces are gymnasium Tuples, so the bridge derives structure but no per-element limits from them; the action bounds are documented in the Facts
the MANO model files and the hand-shape randomization are not modelled by the fake; the upstream package requires MANO_MODELS_DIR (README.md:25-29)

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step, reset or seed is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state is kept and stays readable
